qt: to the Commission Friedrich Pürner (NI) Subject:

In its answer to priority question for written answer P-003206/20261, the Commission fails to address the significant discrepancies between EU Internal Affairs and Migration Commissioner Magnus Brunner’s statement of 31 July 2026 and the subsequent findings of the Ceuta authorities. Furthermore, the answer contains neither specific details regarding the administrative and reporting level of the Spanish authorities at which the underlying information was collected, nor an assessment of the discrepancies referred to. 1.
Before these statements were published, did the Commission or Frontex carry out an independent plausibility check on the primary data collected by the Spanish authorities?

In view of the discrepancy between the claim of 31 July 2026 that practically all those who had entered Ceuta illegally had been returned to Morocco and the information of 3 August 2026 from the Ceuta authorities that between 3000 and 5000 persons still remained illegally on the territory, has clarification or a correction of the information provided been requested from the Spanish Government?

What documented data – in particular Eurodac comparisons, biometric registrations or other registration data – did the Commission rely on to reach its finding that landings in mainland Spain were not linked to the events at the border section of Ceuta and that there were no linked internal migrations?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.11.2026) The public remark made by the Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration on 31 July 2026 reflected the only information available at that time, which relied on the information provided by Spanish authorities. Since the events in Ceuta, the Commission has been in close contact with the Spanish authorities at political and technical levels. Through the EU Migration Preparedness and Crisis Blueprint Network, which brings together Commission services, the European External Action Service, Member States, EU agencies, and international organisations to exchange information on migratory developments, Spanish authorities have been providing updated data on the evolution of the situation and the estimated number of irregular migrants present in Ceuta. The Commission has not received information by Spain and EU agencies confirming media reports on unauthorised movements to mainland Spain. Due to the specific situation of Ceuta and Melilla in the Schengen area, as provided for by Article 41 of Regulation (EU) 2016/3991, checks are carried between Ceuta and Melilla, and the Spanish mainland, thereby preventing onward movements and preserving the integrity of the Schengen area.
1 Regulation (EU) 2016/399 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2016 on a Union Code
on the rules governing the movement of persons across borders (Schengen Borders Code) (codification), OJ L 77, 23.3.2016, pp. 1 (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/399/oj).
